messages:
maddie: Heads-up — ran AWQ + GPTQ comparison on atlas-qa with continuous batching + prefix KV cache enabled. Seeing KV hit-rate drop for AWQ and a 2-3% MMLU delta vs float16. Sharing quick traces and notes.

reza: Can you drop the perf numbers + prefix-hit histogram?

maddie: Sure. Ran 50k inferences (mixed prompt lengths). Config:
```
model: llama-70b
variants: float16, gptq-8bit, awq-8bit
batching: continuous
batch_window_ms: 8
prefetch: enabled
kvcache: prefix + prefix_hashing=v1
```

maddie: Raw summary (median of 3 runs):
- float16 MMLU: 78.3
- gptq-8 MMLU: 77.6 (−0.7)
- awq-8  MMLU: 76.1 (−2.2)

maddie: KV cache hit-rate by model (same workload):
- float16: 0.72
- gptq-8: 0.68
- awq-8: 0.60

ci-bot: perf job 2026-03-15T10:12Z finished — artifacts https://ci.internal/runs/1915123456

oliver: :eyes: That's a pretty big hit for AWQ. Do we know if prefix hashing produced different fingerprints? Could be quantization changing tokenization/embedding leading to different key sequences.

maddie: I checked. Fingerprint counts (unique prefix hashes / total prefixes):
- float16: 0.42
- gptq-8: 0.44
- awq-8: 0.49

maddie: AWQ shows ~+7% unique prefixes -> more misses, looks like KV collisions/normalization issue or slight numeric divergence causing early mismatch.

sophia: Also check evict/ttl behavior under continuous batching. If AWQ has slightly longer per-token latency, continuous batching could change when prefixes are inserted vs read.

dave: Good point. Can you reproduce single-worker deterministic to eliminate scheduling noise? Also run with batch_window_ms=0 (disable continuous batching) to compare.

maddie: Re-ran small reproducer (10k queries) single-worker + `--batch_window_ms=0`:
- float16 hit: 0.73
- awq-8  hit: 0.71
- awq delta on MMLU narrowed to −0.9

maddie: So continuous batching + AWQ amplifies hit-rate drop vs strict batching.

reza: Hypothesis: AWQ alters attention/kvcache key ordering or numeric near-equality used in hashing; continuous batching interleaves writes/reads so mismatches surface as misses. Any diffs in the kv key bytes?

maddie: Dumped first 200 prefix keys for a few requests — gist: https://internal/gists/awq-kv-keys (redacted)

oliver: If keys differ by a few low-order bits due to fp quant noise, our prefix hashing/v1 that takes raw bytes will treat them as different. We should either normalize keys (hash on token ids + layer idx) or use a quantization-insensitive fingerprint (e.g., apply Murmur on rounded floats).

sophia: Before changing fingerprinting, quick mitigation: increase prefetch granularity and relax eviction threshold so short prefixes get cached longer. That should help canary traffic while we root-cause.

maddie: Quick test: bumped prefetch_size from 8 -> 20, eviction_thresh 0.15 -> 0.05 — AWQ hit went 0.60 -> 0.68, MMLU delta improved from −2.2 to −1.1. Latency 95p +8ms.

dave: That's promising as a temporary config change. We must track cost/latency tradeoff. Add to rollout checklist.

reza: Long-term fix: change KV fingerprint to (token_seq, layer, head_meta) or stable hash over token IDs + quantization bucket. I can prototype.

oliver: Also run a cross-quant bakeoff with batch_window_ms sweep [0,4,8,16] because continuous batching change is a major lever. Document interaction effects (hit-rate x latency x accuracy).

maddie: Agreed. Proposed action items:
- reza: prototype stable fingerprint (token-id-based) + bench (A)
- oliver: run batch_window sweep on three quant variants (float16, gptq-8, awq-8) (B)
- sophia: add a short eval set (prefetch-sensitive queries) to our regression alerts (C)
- dave: prepare canary config (prefetch_size=20, eviction_thresh=0.05) and fallback to float16

sophia: For (C) put thresholds: MMLU drop >0.8 OR kvcache-hit delta >0.05 => rollback. Also wire an automated alert for 95p latency +30ms.

maddie: I'll kick off B now and attach logs. Reza ping me when prototype ready and I'll run the same workload.

maddie: Thanks all. If we want to triage faster, we can gate AWQ on dedicated pool without continuous batching until fingerprint patch is in.

oliver: Sounds good. :thumbsup: \n
ci-bot: created issue #MLINF-982: "AWQ kvcache hit instability under continuous batching" (assignee: reza)

maddie: Closing loop — I'll post final numbers + canary plan in this thread when B finishes.
